scope.description: Local timeout-to-contact-to-lease comparison under explicitly constructed local state, using actual in-memory transport completion and actual Raft consumers.
assumptions: Exactly two Voters, local node and one remote peer; no membership change.
Node initially has local Leader state and a peer-contact marker older than LeaderLeaseTimeout; this is an assumed local prefix, not a claimed elected state.
No receiver Raft processes the queued request and no reply is sent; no other writer changes contact.
Lease check runs after the tested timeout consumer completes; omitted background workers isolate this conditional effect.
excluded: Proof of a legal election/startup history
Automatic lease scheduling or total role-retention duration
Application stale reads, client success, or incorrect log commitment

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: Construct local Raft state directly rather than bootstrap/elect; this is the accepted conditional premise.
Receiver transport has no receiver Raft worker and sends no response. This prevents new contact independently of the tested marker.
Call pipelineDecode/replicateTo and checkLeaderLease explicitly; omit main loop, heartbeat, snapshots and verification to isolate effect. This does not establish deployed role retention.
Read LastContact under its lock and State through public API; only emit measured fields and declared setup. No protocol source is modified.
boundaries: Proof of a legal election/startup history
Automatic lease scheduling or total role-retention duration
Application stale reads, client success, or incorrect log commitment
Operation labels associate separate scenarios, not one shared history.
The prior contact is constructed as expired; no legal full-node initial prefix is proved.
No claim that rejecting a real heartbeat response is required: no-response and negative-response are different contexts.
Whether this conditional prefix occurs in one legal full-node history with protective workers active.
Whether a single refresh postpones externally observable leadership loss; the local invocation alone establishes neither a timing bound nor an application failure.
